title: A Walk through a Museum
description: Visit a museum gallery through the words for displays, descriptive signs, and the people who help visitors understand them.
cardDescription: Visit a museum gallery through the words for displays, descriptive signs, and the people who help visitors understand them.
focus: A museum object, the room around it, and the information beside it serve different roles. Several ordinary words acquire a specific meaning in this visitor setting.
solvingTip: Decide whether the definition asks for a person, an object, a place, or written information. That choice narrows the longer answers.
words: DOCENT
Museum guide who explains collections to visitors
ARTIFACT
Object made or used by people and preserved for study
GALLERY
Museum room or area where works are displayed
LABEL
Small written panel identifying a museum object
MODEL
Small-scale representation used to explain a larger subject
EXHIBIT
Single presented object or organized museum presentation
CASE
Protective glass enclosure around a museum item
DISPLAY
Arrangement of objects presented for museum visitors to see
GUIDE
Person or booklet helping a visitor follow a museum route
TICKET
Admission document checked at a museum entrance
MAP
Diagram showing the locations of museum rooms
ROOM
Separate enclosed space within the museum building
HALL
Large passage or entrance space inside a museum
VISITOR
Person who comes to view a museum's collections

answerNotes.DOCENT: A docent guides or teaches visitors. The term describes a role and does not by itself specify whether the person is paid or a volunteer.
answerNotes.ARTIFACT: An artifact is an object connected with human activity. It differs from a purely natural specimen such as an unworked mineral.
answerNotes.GALLERY: Gallery can name an exhibition space. It is different from the label beside an individual object.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label often gives an object's name, maker, date, or context. It is information about the item rather than the item itself.
answerNotes.MODEL: A model represents something else. A museum may use one to show a building, machine, or historical scene.

title: A Botanical Garden Visit
description: Stroll among plant collections and learn the names used for distinctive growth forms and garden structures.
cardDescription: Stroll among plant collections and learn the names used for distinctive growth forms and garden structures.
focus: A botanical garden groups plants for display and study. The clues distinguish related plant categories, including cacti within the larger succulent grouping and bamboo within the grasses.
solvingTip: Use the defining plant feature or structure. A storage habit, a leaf shape, and a growing shelter lead to different answers.
words: GREENHOUSE
Glass or translucent building used to grow protected plants
SUCCULENT
Plant with fleshy tissue adapted to storing water
CACTUS
Succulent plant group whose members have specialized areoles
FERN
Frond-bearing plant that reproduces by spores rather than seeds
BAMBOO
Tall jointed-stemmed plant belonging to the grass family
ORCHID
Flowering plant group including moth ___ varieties
PALM
Tree or shrub group often bearing large fanlike or featherlike leaves
MOSS
Small nonflowering plant forming soft green mats
BED
Prepared planting area beside a garden path
LABEL
Plant-identification marker beside a botanical specimen
PATH
Walking route through the garden's collections
SEED
Reproductive structure from which a flowering plant can grow
FROND
Large divided leaf of a fern or palm
TROPICAL
Describing plants native to warm regions near the equator

answerNotes.GREENHOUSE: A greenhouse provides a protected growing environment. Its temperature and growing conditions depend on its design and operation.
answerNotes.SUCCULENT: Many succulents store water in leaves or stems. Cacti are one succulent group, but not every succulent is a cactus.
answerNotes.CACTUS: Areoles are the characteristic structures from which cactus spines, branches, or flowers can develop. Some cacti have few or no obvious spines.
answerNotes.FERN: Ferns reproduce using spores. They do not produce flowers and seeds in the way flowering garden plants do.
answerNotes.BAMBOO: Bamboo is a grass despite its woody-looking stems. The growth form can make that relationship surprising.

title: At the Neighborhood Craft Fair
description: Browse a local fair through handmade objects, market spaces, and the everyday vocabulary of buying a small gift.
cardDescription: Browse a local fair through handmade objects, market spaces, and the everyday vocabulary of buying a small gift.
focus: This scene centers on makers and their work rather than a particular holiday. Material and process words help distinguish a finished object from the craft used to create it.
solvingTip: A clue may name what an object is made from, how it is produced, or where it is sold. Use the category to find the answer.
words: POTTERY
Objects shaped from clay and hardened by firing
WEAVING
Craft of interlacing strands to make a fabric or basket surface
STALL
Small open selling space at a fair
CANDLE
Wax object with a wick, often sold by a craft maker
PRINT
Artwork made by transferring an inked image to paper
BOOTH
Vendor's enclosed or partly enclosed stand at a craft fair
CRAFT
Skilled activity producing a handmade decorative or useful object
SOAP
Cleansing bar a maker may scent and wrap by hand
WOOD
Material carved or turned by a fair's furniture maker
BASKET
Woven container offered at a handmade-goods stall
CARD
Folded paper greeting decorated by a local maker
PRICE
Amount shown on a craft item's sales tag
CASH
Physical money used to pay at a market stall
CHANGE
Money returned when a payment exceeds the selling amount
YARN
Spun strand sold by a fiber artist at a craft fair
ART
Creative work displayed by a local maker
BEAD
Small pierced decorative piece used in handmade jewelry
TOY
Handmade plaything offered at a woodworker's stall
SIGN
Written notice naming a fair vendor or a price

answerNotes.POTTERY: Pottery begins with clay and is hardened by firing. The word can also refer to the craft or a workshop producing it.
answerNotes.WEAVING: Weaving crosses sets of strands. Knitting instead forms fabric through interlocking loops.
answerNotes.STALL: A stall is a vendor's selling space. Its exact construction can range from a simple table to a more substantial enclosure.
answerNotes.CANDLE: The wick carries melted wax to the flame when a candle burns. The finished object is different from a bar of decorative soap.
answerNotes.PRINT: A print is produced through a transfer process. The term differs from an original drawing made directly on the sheet.
answerNotes.YARN: Yarn is a continuous strand of fibers used in crafts such as knitting and weaving. It is a material rather than a finished garment.
answerNotes.ART: Art names creative work here. The clue uses a broad category rather than a particular material or technique.
answerNotes.BEAD: A bead commonly has a hole allowing it to be threaded. It is one component of a handmade ornament rather than the whole accessory.

title: The Community Bandstand
description: Picture a public park concert through its open-air performance structure, surrounding paths, and audience.
cardDescription: Picture a public park concert through its open-air performance structure, surrounding paths, and audience.
focus: A bandstand provides a place for performers, while nearby park features serve walkers and listeners. Some structures have several shapes, so the clues focus on use rather than an assumed number of sides.
solvingTip: Read the role of each park feature. A roofed structure, a boundary, and a place to sit ask for different objects.
words: BANDSTAND
Raised outdoor platform or structure for musical performances
GAZEBO
Open-sided roofed garden or park shelter
RAILING
Protective barrier along the edge of a raised platform
APPLAUSE
Audience's clapping after a park performance
CONCERT
Musical performance presented to an audience
ROOF
Overhead covering sheltering the park musicians
STEP
Single level climbed to reach a raised stage
PARK
Public green space containing this performance area
LAWN
Area of closely cut grass where listeners may gather
BENCH
Long outdoor seat beside the concert lawn
PATH
Walkway leading toward the performance shelter
MUSIC
Organized sound heard from the community ensemble
PICNIC
Outdoor meal enjoyed before a park performance
FLAG
Fabric emblem flying near a public park's entrance

answerNotes.BANDSTAND: A bandstand is intended for performers. It may have a roof, but its purpose rather than one fixed shape defines it.
answerNotes.GAZEBO: A gazebo is a shelter or viewpoint. Gazebos can have different shapes and do not all have eight sides.
answerNotes.RAILING: A railing forms a barrier beside an edge or stair. It is distinct from the roof overhead.
answerNotes.APPLAUSE: Applause is a response from listeners. It differs from the music produced by the performers.
answerNotes.CONCERT: A concert describes an event, while a bandstand is the place that may host it.

title: At the County History Room
description: Explore local history through records, photographs, and the filing words used to organize a community collection.
cardDescription: Explore local history through records, photographs, and the filing words used to organize a community collection.
focus: Different records preserve different evidence. A census, a deed, and a diary have separate purposes, while indexes and folders help a visitor find material within a collection.
solvingTip: Match the document with its job. A population record is different from a land document or a person’s daily account.
words: CENSUS
Official count of a population, often preserved as historical records
ARCHIVE
Collection or repository of preserved records
DEED
Legal document associated with transferring property ownership
DIARY
Personal written account arranged by days
INDEX
Alphabetical or other ordered guide to names or subjects in records
RECORD
Preserved document providing evidence of an event
MAP
Drawn representation of a county's roads or boundaries
PHOTO
Short word for an image captured by a camera
LETTER
Written personal message preserved in a history collection
DATE
Calendar identification of when a document was created
COPY
Reproduction made from an original historical document
FOLDER
Paper holder keeping related records together
CLERK
Official or employee maintaining public documents
COUNTY
Local governmental area whose history fills this room

answerNotes.CENSUS: A census records population information at a particular time. Its questions and surviving records vary by place and period.
answerNotes.ARCHIVE: An archive holds records kept for their continuing value. The word can name either the collection or the place maintaining it.
answerNotes.DEED: A deed concerns property rights. It is different from a general map showing where land lies.
answerNotes.DIARY: A diary records an individual's observations or activities. It provides a different perspective from an official population count.
answerNotes.INDEX: An index helps locate information within a larger collection. It is not itself necessarily the original historical document.
